sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition to recall the records and set aside the award dated 03.11.2020 and amendment award dated 22.12.2020 passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator,
Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 92 / 2011-12 in respect of schedule property and also to direct the Arbitrator to reconsider the A.P. No.95/2022 compensation as per the present market value and further to enhance the compensation as per the materials available on record before the Court by increasing the market value for the acquired land and also such other reliefs.
.2.

The definite case of the petitioners is that the property bearing Sy. No.35 measuring 3228 Sq. feet of Sonnappanahalli village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 30.07.2010 Subsequently the respondent No.2/LAO
has awarded a total sum of Rs.48,37,644/- for 3228 Sq. feet of land.
The petitioner received the same under protest and filed an application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.10,000/- per Sq. feet as on 12.03.2012.

Accordingly,
the said application taken by the respondent No. 3 for consideration.

.3. In the said petition, the respondent No.2 filed statement of objection stating that the contention urged A.P. No.95/2022 by the petitioner are baseless and the same are made without any substance.
The petitioner has not produced any relevant documents to justify their claim for enhanced compensation and the claim of the petitioners cannot be sustained in law.
Hence, question of enhancement of compensation will not arise and the claim of the petitioner is liable to be dismissed by the respondent No.2.
Accordingly, prayed to dismiss the reference.

.4. Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed order in LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 91 / 92 /2011-12, 189/130/53/2012-13, 21/22/23/7/2014- 15 dated 03.11.2020, which is amended subsequently on 22.12.2020.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioners filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :

A.P. No.95/2022 :GROUNDS:
The impugned award passed by the Special Deputy Commission er and the Arbitrator is wholly erroneous, contrary to law, materials on record and in violation of principles of natural justice and the same is liable to be set aside.

The Arbitrator committed a legal misconduct in not following the documents filed by the petitioner for deciding the market value and enhancing the market value in the proceedings before him while passing the impugned award.
Further the Arbitrator has not followed the procedure prescribed in the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
The award dated 02.04.2011 passed by the respondent No.2 is not passed in accordance with the guidelines under Section 3G(7) of NH Act.
The entire proceedings culminated in passing the award are vitiated.
The Arbitrator grossly erred in considering the fact that the acquired land situated very near to Bengaluru International Airport and situated amidst the lands commercially developed.

The Arbitrator A.P. No.95/2022 has failed to appreciate that the respondents have not produced any document to justify his award and on what basis he has awarded the low compensation amount and the award amount is not at all matching with the market value for this prime land.
The respondent No.2 is unjustified and it is not at all fair enough to compensate the loss incurred by the petitioner.

The Arbitrator grossly erred in law in not addressing all the terms of reference and the Arbitrator in the impugned award has miserable failed to address various aspects such as adequacy of compensation awarded to the petitioner by taking into consideration various special features such as strategic location of the project, prevailing market value and conversion of lands in question for non- agricultural purposes, compensation awarded by other authorities etc., and the petitioner is entitled for payment of solatium on the award amount and additional market value along with interest from the date of taking A.P.
No.95/2022 possession till the date of payment and among other lands, prayed to allow the petition.
.6.

The respondent No.1 filed a detailed objections claiming that the application is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the respondent No. 3 passed the award as per the guidance value produced before the Arbitrator pertaining to the year 2011.
The petitioner is attempting to mislead this Court by drawing reference to incorrect/wholly inapplicable guidance notification.
The respondent No.1 totally denied all the grounds claimed by the petitioner in the petition.

The Arbitrator/ respondent No. 3 passed the award after giving full opportunity of hearing to the petitioner by considering the material evidence on record for enhancement of compensation together with all other statutory benefits available under the LA Act in accordance with law and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
A.P. No.95/2022 .7.
The petitioner along with the petition filed I.A. No.1 under Section 34(3) of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, for condonation of delay if any filing the petition.

sentences.text: The above application is supported with the affidavit of GPA holder of petitioner, wherein, he has stated that his property has been acquired by the respondents and the matter was referred to the Arbitrator for arbitration.
The Arbitrator never recorded any evidence nor the order was communicated to him.

The impugned order has not been communicated to him and subsequently when he approached the concerned authority on 18.04.2022, he came to know about the order and he immediately applied for copy of the order and he got the same on 26.05.2022.
Thereafter, filed this petition and accordingly prayed for condonation of delay if any in filing the petition.
.9. The respondent No.1 has not filed any objections to the IA.
.10. The respondent No.1 though served with the notice appeared before the Court.
The respondent No.2 A.P. No.95/2022 though served with the notice, not chosen to appear before the Court to resist the petition and hence, the respondent No.2 has been placed exparte.
The respondent No. 3 appeared before the Court through DGP.

The entire records in LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 91 / 92 /
2011-12, 189 / 130 / 53 / 2012-13, 21 / 22 / 23 / 7 /2014-15 dated 03.11.2020, which is amended subsequently on 22.12.2020 secured from the Arbitrator.
.11.

On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
1) Whether the petition filed by the petitioner is within time ?
2) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
3) What order or award?
.12.
Heard the arguments.

The petitioner has produced the citations i.e., (1) Union of India Vs.
Tarsem Singh in No. Civil Appeal No. 7064/2019 A.P. No.95/2022 (Arising out of SLP(C) No. 9599 of 2019); (2) NHAI Vs. P. Nagaraju @ Cheluvaiah and another in No. SLP (C) No. 19775/2021 (2022 LiveLaw (SC) 584); (3) The SLAO and another Vs. Sri. Muthaiah and another in MFA No.
2930/2020; (4) D.S. Gopal Krishna Vs. The Project Director and General Manager and others in A.P. No. 15045/2022; (5) NHAI and another Vs. The Additional Commissioner and others in A.A.
No. 03 of 2022; and (6) The Hon'ble Supreme Court, judgment dated 08.03.2021 in Suo Motu Writ Petition (Civil) No. 3 of 2020 with respect to COGNIGANCE FOR EXTENSION OF LIMITATION extending the limitation period of 90 days from 01.03.2022.

sentences.text: Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note an admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The petitioner is the owner of the property bearing Sy. No.35 measuring 3228 Sq. feets of Sonnappanahalli village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 30.07.2010
, is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.2/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs.1,314/- per Sq. feet for the acquired land.

entities.text: Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.48,37,644/- being the land value was disbursed to the petitioner as compensation.
The petitioner received the same under protest and filed an application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.10,000/- per Sq. feet as on 12.03.2012.
Accordingly, the said application is taken by the respondent No. 3 for consideration.

.16. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the petitioner filed an application before the respondent No.3 claiming that he is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.10,000/- per Sq. feet as on 12.03.2012.

On basis of the said application, the respondent No.3 hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 91 A.P. No.95/2022 92 / 2011-12, 189 / 130 / 53 / 2012-13,
21 / 22 / 23 / 7 / 2014-15 dated 03.11.2020, which is amended subsequently on 22.12.2020.

The respondent No.3 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.2,625/- per Sq. feet from Rs.1,314/- per Sq.feet and awarded additional compensation of Rs.1,311/- per Sq. meter.
.17.
The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.3 without considering the documentary evidence placed by the petitioner and also without considering the claim of the petitioner that other properties have enhanced the market value which is much higher than the compensation enhanced by the respondent No. 3.
The said claim of the petitioner is also found in the award.

On close perusal of the order passed by the respondent No. 3, it is clear that the respondent No. 3 considering the guidance value of the year 2010-11 published vide notification bearing No. CVC 19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011 enhanced the compensation, but there is no A.P. No.95/2022 material on record to show that the petitioner has produced the alleged documents claimed by the petitioner in the petition for perusal of Arbitrator/respondent No. 3.
.18.

However, it is the definite case of petitioner that the very same Arbitrator in different cases has enhanced the market value 3 times and such enhancement of compensation not given to the petitioner though the property of the petitioner is acquired for National Highways and the said property of the petitioner was abutting to the National Highways.

sentences.text: In support of this contention, the petitioner has produced the copy of the order passed in LAQ/ARB/NH-07/CR/01/2019-20 dated 09.01.2020.
In the said case, the LAO has enhanced the compensation 3 times of the compensation awarded by LAO/ respondent No. 2.
Admittedly in the case on hand, the LAO awarded the compensation of Rs.1,314/- per Sq. feet and it is enhanced to the tune of Rs.2,625/- per Sq. feet by enhancing only Rs.1311/-.
Therefore, the A.P. No.95/2022 claim of the petitioner is probable that the respondent No.3 has not properly appreciated the material placed before him while passing the order.
Apart from that, the impugned order of the respondent No. 3 also does not disclose any reasons for the enhancement made in the impugned award.
The Arbitrator has stated much about contention taken by petitioner and respondent No. 1 in the order and abruptly decided the market value without assigning any proper reasons.
Hence, the order of the LAO certainly liable to be intervened by this court.
Accordingly, the point No.2 is held in the affirmative.
.20. Point No.3:
In view of my above findings, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER IA filed by the petitioner to condone the delay in filing the petition is allowed.
Petition filed under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is hereby allowed.

Consequently, the impugned award passed by the respondent No.3 in case LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/92/2011-12 dated 03.11.2020 amended award dated 22.12.2020 in respect of Sy. No.35 measuring 3228 Sq. feets of Sonnappanahalli village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru Urban District is set aside with liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
Office is directed to send back the Lower Court records.
